transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because work has been feeling… harder than it should, maybe. The district added this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout to my plate, on top of my regular teaching, and I’m still managing to get through the school day, so it’s not like I’m falling apart or anything.

But I do feel more wound up and discouraged than I’m used to, and I’ve noticed I’m putting off lesson plans and emails that I normally would’ve just handled. It’s just not really like me, and I thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets worse, if that makes sense.
Are you still enjoying the things you used to like doing?

I think… mostly, yes. I mean, I haven’t really taken stock of it, honestly. I still like the things I like, as far as I can tell. Maybe I’m just a little less quick to get to them lately, but I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped enjoying them. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?

Yes… I think “on edge” is a fair way to put it. I wouldn’t say I’m panicking or anything like that, and I’m still getting through my school day, but since the district added this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on top of my regular teaching, I do feel more wound up than usual.

And discouraged, too, honestly. I’ve noticed I’m putting off lesson plans and emails that I normally would’ve just handled without thinking much about it. It’s just not very like me. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling sad lately?

Sad… maybe a little, yes. I don’t want to overstate it, because I’m still getting through my teaching day and doing what I need to do. But since this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout got added on top of my regular work, I’ve felt more discouraged than I’m used to.

It’s not like me exactly—I’ve been putting off lesson plans and emails I normally would’ve just handled. So I guess I’d say discouraged more than deeply sad, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight lately?

Not really, no. I mean, I haven’t been tracking it closely or anything, but my clothes seem to fit about the same. I don’t think there’s been any noticeable change. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are there any tasks or situations that you've been avoiding lately?

Yes… a little. I mean, I’m not just ignoring everything, I am still getting through my school day. But I’ve been putting off lesson plans and emails lately, which is unusual for me.

It really seemed to start after the district added that bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on top of my regular teaching. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I feel kind of wound up and discouraged, and those tasks that I normally would’ve handled without a second thought just feel harder to start. Does that answer what you mean?
Are you avoiding social interactions or certain people because of how you've been feeling?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I might be a little quieter than usual sometimes, but I’m not avoiding certain people or canceling things because of it. At least, I haven’t really noticed that. Does that seem like what you’re asking?
Are there things you used to enjoy that you no longer find pleasure in?

I don’t think so, not in a big way. I mean, I still enjoy the things I usually enjoy when I actually do them. Maybe I’m a little less eager to start sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped finding pleasure in them. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling wound up and discouraged?

Probably about five months now… not forever or anything, but since the district assigned me that rollout role midyear. That’s when I started feeling more wound up and discouraged. Does that sound like the kind of timeframe you mean?
Have you felt like you're just going through the motions of daily life without much emotional response?

Not really, no. I mean, I can have days where I’m just doing what needs to get done, but I still feel like myself, and I still react to things. I wouldn’t say I’m numb or anything like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Guilty? Um… not especially, I don’t think. I mean, I can second-guess myself sometimes, like whether I handled something the best way, but I wouldn’t say I’m carrying around a lot of guilt. Is that okay—does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you noticed a decrease in interest in activities or hobbies that you usually find interesting or enjoyable?

I don’t think so, not in a major way. I still enjoy the things I usually enjoy when I actually make time for them. Maybe I’m a little less eager some days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling more tired than usual lately?

Maybe a little here and there, but not dramatically. I’m 56, so sometimes I figure being tired is just part of a busy week, especially with teaching. I wouldn’t say it’s been a big change or anything concerning. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you've been feeling less emotionally responsive to things that would normally affect you, like good or bad news?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I still react to things—if something good happens I’m happy, and if something upsetting happens, it does get to me. Maybe I try to keep things steady, especially at work, but I wouldn’t say I feel numb or anything like that. Does that answer it?
Do you feel like you've been feeling disconnected from your emotions or the people around you?

No, I don’t think so. I still feel connected to people around me, and I can tell what I’m feeling most of the time. Maybe I keep things to myself a bit, but I wouldn’t say I feel disconnected, if that’s what you mean.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy doing most of the time over the past few months?

Not really, I don’t think so. I still enjoy the things I usually like when I get the chance. Maybe some days I don’t get around to them as much, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest most of the time. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since you started feeling wound up and discouraged?

No, I don’t think so. My weight’s been about the same as far as I can tell. Maybe it goes up or down a little like normal, but nothing significant that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you felt like your wound-up and discouraged feelings have been interfering with your relationships or daily activities in a significant way?

A little, yes… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I’m still teaching and I am getting the basic things done. But I’ve noticed I’m not as on top of planning as I usually am. I’ve missed or pushed back a few planning deadlines, and a couple of colleagues have had to remind me about things I used to just handle on my own. So… it is affecting my day-to-day work some, I guess.
Would you say that your feelings of being wound up and discouraged have caused significant problems in your relationships or daily activities?

Yes… I mean, not in a severe way, I don’t think. I’m still teaching and getting my main responsibilities done. But it has caused some problems, mostly with keeping up with planning. I’ve missed or pushed back a few deadlines, and colleagues have had to remind me about things I used to handle pretty reliably on my own. So… I guess it is interfering some.
Have you ever had a period of two weeks or more where you felt depressed most of the day?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most of the day for two full weeks, no. I’ve had stretches where I felt pretty discouraged or worn down, but… not like I was down all day every day for that long, if that makes sense.
